prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer looks down at their own hands and forearms at the bottom-center (roughly 0.4–0.6 metres away) and another person's lower legs and bare feet extending from the top-left (about 0.6–1.2 metres away) onto a cushioned footrest directly in front of the wearer, all above a background floor roughly 1.2–1.5 metres below the camera. The seated person faces toward the camera wearer with their upper torso and head out of view beyond the top-left edge, while the wearer's hands are in direct contact (0 metres separation) with the person's left foot and cotton ball within immediate arm's reach, partially occluding the left toes and white towel underneath. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's head tilts slightly up and to the left in frames 2–4 before returning right in frame 5, bringing the bright white side table on the far left (roughly 0.4–0.5 metres away) into view in frames 2–5 as the right hand shifts slightly away from the toes in frames 4–5. Compared to the busy patterned terrazzo floor in RGB, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground table edge, hands, legs, and footrest from the flat floor plane, though it is unreliable in frame 1 where the floor depth is inconsistently bright compared to frames 2–5 and along the bottom-left beneath the table where floor regions drop to near-black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the seated person's legs and feet extending from the upper-left toward the lower-center (0.6–1.2 metres from the camera wearer) and parts of the camera wearer's own hands and arms at the bottom-center (0.4–0.6 metres away), all within the wearer's arm's reach while the other person's upper body remains out of frame at the top-left. In frame 1, two distinct `person` masks separate the seated person's legs (pink, upper-left) from the camera wearer's hands and lap/footrest area (brown, lower-center/right) where the hands overlap and occlude the left foot at 0 metres separation. Across frames 2 to 5, as the camera view shifts slightly and the wearer's hands adjust position around the left foot, both individuals are merged into a single pink `person` mask that intermittently includes parts of the side table on the left in frames 2 and 5. While this map highlights the contour of the two parallel lower legs against the complex floor and chair background, it is highly unreliable: it merges the two separate people and the white towel/footrest into one instance in frames 2–5, completely misses the camera wearer's hands in frames 3–4, and hallucinates a large blue `giraffe` mask over the patterned terrazzo floor on the right side of frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints in the lower-center foreground (0.4–0.8 metres from the camera wearer), where the seated person's bare feet rest side-by-side in front of the wearer and within immediate arm's reach while both individuals' heads and torsos remain out of view (preventing gaze detection from the map alone, though the legs face toward the wearer). It reveals fine joint articulations of the digits that are somewhat blended in the RGB image, specifically showing the two parallel yellow lower-leg lines extending from the upper-left down to the ankles in frame 3. However, the map is largely unreliable because it consistently misclassifies the seated person's bare feet and ten toes as magenta hand skeletons across all five frames, and only detects one of the camera wearer's actual hands (lower-right, 0.4–0.5 metres away) in frame 4 while missing both hands in frames 1–3 and 5. Furthermore, in frames 3–5 it produces tangled, inverted yellow body-skeleton boxes and stray facial/torso keypoints clustered around the wearer's hands and the seated person's left foot where the hands occlude the toes, failing to maintain consistent body tracking across the slight camera pan and hand movements.
